questions.q: Why is a slow ACL script a more serious performance concern than a slow scheduled job that runs once a night?
options: ACL scripts always run with elevated database permissions
ACL scripts run on every access attempt to the governed record or field -- every form load, list view, and API call -- so the delay compounds across the whole instance
Scheduled jobs are not allowed to contain any script logic
There is no real difference in performance impact between the two
questions.explain: A scheduled job's cost is paid once per run. An ACL script's cost is paid on every single access attempt it governs, all day, for every user.

questions.q:
What does this corrected version of the same check do, and why is it preferred?
```javascript
answer = gs.getUser().isMemberOf('a1b2c3d4e5f6a7b8c9d0e1f2a3b4c5d6');
```
options: It checks group membership using GlideUser's already-cached data for the transaction, avoiding a fresh database query
It is functionally different from the GlideRecord version and checks role, not group membership
It only works for the admin role
It is slower than the GlideRecord version because it loads the full user record
questions.explain: gs.getUser() returns a GlideUser object that already holds role and group membership data for the current transaction; isMemberOf() reuses it instead of querying again.

questions.q: An ACL needs to check whether the current record's state equals 3. What's the fastest way to express that in the script?
options: Query the table again with a GlideRecord to re-read the state field
Compare current.state directly, since the record is already loaded into memory for the ACL check
Call gs.getUser() to look up the record's state
It cannot be checked inside an ACL script at all
questions.explain: current already represents the record being evaluated -- comparing its fields directly avoids any unnecessary query.

questions.q: What is the general guidance this lesson gives for writing ACL scripts?
options: Always query related tables directly for the most accurate, real-time answer
Keep ACL scripts fast and simple, preferring already-available data (current's fields, gs.getUser()) over querying other tables
ACL scripts should never contain any conditional logic
Performance doesn't matter for ACL scripts since they run server-side
questions.explain: Because ACL scripts run so frequently, the standard guidance is to favor cheap, already-cached data over fresh queries whenever possible.
